title: How computers work
examples: Does the computer think for itself?
What is the difference between RAM and hard drive?
How does the computer understand pictures?

explain.say: A computer needs ways to get information into it. This is called input.
The computer's brain takes the input and changes it. This is the processing stage.
After thinking, the computer shows you the result. This is the output.
Computers must remember things for later use. This is called storage.
Computers only understand on or off signals. We call this binary code.
When you type the letter A, the computer processes it into binary code. This is 01000001.

faq.q: What is the difference between RAM and long-term storage?
faq.a: RAM is like your desk where you work right now; it holds things temporarily. Hard drives are like filing cabinets that keep things safe for a long time.
asks: Where does the computer keep things while it runs?
Is RAM for saving or for working?

faq.q: Why do computers use binary code?
faq.a: Computers are made of electrical switches that are either on or off. These two states match the numbers one and zero.
asks: Why can't they use letters and numbers directly?
What does '1' mean in a computer?

faq.q: Does the CPU do all the thinking?
faq.a: The CPU is the main component that performs calculations and follows instructions. It directs the whole process of the computer.
asks: Is the CPU the boss of the computer?
What is the job of the CPU?

faq.q: What is the difference between input and output devices?
faq.a: Input devices send information to the computer, like a microphone. Output devices take information out, like speakers.
asks: What is the job of a printer?

faq.q: What is the role of the operating system?
faq.a: The operating system manages all the hardware and software so that different parts can talk to each other correctly.
asks: How does the computer know what to do?

facts: Input devices send data to the computer.
The CPU processes the data received from input.
Output devices show the results to the user.
Binary code uses only two digits: one and zero.

quiz.say: If you speak into a microphone, which part of the computer process is happening?
quiz.why: The microphone sends sound data into the computer system.

wrong.0: Processing happens after the data has been received by the CPU.
wrong.1: Output is what the computer shows to you, not what you send in.
wrong.2: Storage is for keeping data, not for sending it in.

quiz.say: When a computer plays music through speakers, what stage is this?
quiz.why: Speakers take the processed sound data and make it audible for us to hear.

wrong.0: Input is when you send sound data into the computer.
wrong.1: Processing is the action the CPU takes with the sound data.
wrong.2: Storage keeps the music file, but the speakers are showing it.

quiz.say: The letter 'B' is represented in binary code by:
quiz.why: This sequence of ones and zeros is the computer's way of writing the letter B.

wrong.0: This pattern does not match the binary code for the letter B.
wrong.1: Zeroes mean the computer is not receiving any signal.
wrong.2: All ones would represent a very different character.
